correctness.rationale: Exact stationary two-state edge transition formula (1), exact tagged-vertex factorization (3), and fixed-tag asymptotics (4) imply the Poisson block-profile limit by finite inclusion-exclusion and mixed factorial moments. The necessary limiting one-edge expansions are uniform for each fixed finite sample, and no finite checker is used as a substitute for the argument.

originality.rationale: The 2013 sharp threshold theorem identifies the 1/log n transition but neither states nor implies the exact multitime Poisson signature means or the stationary immigration–death finite-dimensional law. Static isolation Poisson results and dynamic flooding results cover different statistical quantities. The closest published manuscripts inspected have different models (geometric circle, monotone bipartite arrivals, fixed-edge static motifs). value.rationale: Existing sharp noise-sensitivity results identify the inverse-logarithmic scale but leave the conditional persistence and reappearance of rare isolation defects quantitatively unspecified. The complete exact temporal-signature law classifies all multitime dependence, has an interpretable immigration–death mechanism, and gives joint connectivity probabilities, a natural measure of resilience under edge refresh at threshold. It is not a numerical parameter increment or an arbitrary finite slice.
